purpose: Keep candidate admission, field scoring and diagnostic evidence consistent while recovering document-level context across section boundaries.

matching.normalization: Unicode-aware normalized terms with stable token boundaries.
matching.exact: Exact terms and identifiers retain higher evidence than broad partial matches.
matching.prefix: Prefix completion is bounded and used only where the query form permits it.

compoundBriefRetention.activation: During fallback for queries with at least eight term groups, a bounded row matching every query group retains priority over partial rows when candidates compete for retention or selection. Matches using a Markdown indexed_text body keep ordinary scoring, so incidental prose cannot suppress focused headings.
compoundBriefRetention.scope: Ordinary generated-index and source-scan Brief, including document-planner evidence; explicit owner and first-term scope routes keep their existing policies.
compoundBriefRetention.boundary: Explicit lifecycle/authority penalties prevent this priority. Field scores, candidate admission, row provenance, type diversity, per-document limits and output budgets remain unchanged. Additional partial evidence remains eligible; a full match is lexical support, not proof of a complete answer.

jsonKeyPolicy.scanner: JsonKeySpan is an O(n), line-oriented lexical-balanced scanner. A key span includes its own scalar value line or balanced container subtree and ends on the matching close line; subsequent sibling lines are not appended.
jsonKeyPolicy.strings: Quoted braces and escaped quotes are ignored while balancing delimiters, so braces inside JSON strings cannot close a container early.
jsonKeyPolicy.boundary: The span extractor is line-oriented range extraction, not full JSON validation or column-precise AST ownership. Multiple members sharing a line remain line-granular. It makes no malformed-JSON validation claim.

sectionPublication.registeredFormats: Explicitly enrolled .mdc documents use the existing Markdown pipeline, case-insensitively, with original paths and ranges. Profiles own enrollment; hidden directories are not discovered implicitly. globs and alwaysApply remain client metadata, not executed policy or authority. Rebuild earlier .mdc publications explicitly; generator-v20 format is unchanged.
sectionPublication.shape: Existing Markdown section, chunk and document rows retain their original ranges. indexed_text is the normalized, redacted body, separate from the compact preview; no new paragraph rows are introduced.
sectionPublication.matching: Nonempty indexed_text replaces preview in the shared publication/scoring projection at weight 16. Empty fields retain preview matching. Selection policy is documented separately in documentCandidates.
sectionPublication.allocation: Allocate in existing source row order, including overlapping sections/chunks. Redact the complete body before whitespace-boundary clipping, preserving UTF-8 and whole tokens.
sectionPublication.omission: indexed_text_omitted_bytes counts normalized redacted bytes omitted from this field, saturated at INT_MAX. It is not a raw-source byte count or coverage by other records. JSON sections publish empty text and zero omissions.
sectionPublication.identity: Search-only text and omissions participate in typed equality, independent retrieval-unit keys, deterministic ordering and full canonical Pack identity before display projection. Resident and disk readers use the same strict decoder.

retrievalUnits.declaration: The verified manifest sources array declares document kind. Only markdown and json documents permit whole-document corroboration. JSONL rows and source-fact records are independent units; extension guessing or consumer vocabulary is not used.
retrievalUnits.identity: Whole-document units are separated by path, evidence_kind, verification_level, authority_level and status. Independent units additionally retain exact decoded record content, origin and ranges, including SectionRow indexed_text and indexed_text_omitted_bytes. Equal previews never authorize merging distinct independent searchable records. Source facts remain independent even when their physical path is also enrolled as a document.
retrievalUnits.factDeduplication: FactRow uses C++20 defaulted field-by-field comparison for exact deduplication, without serializing lookup keys. Exact decoded copies can merge; differing paths, ranges, origins, statuses, authority or contents cannot. A generic fact with an explicit source and its lossy typed projection are not exact copies and remain distinct candidates. Final output budgets still apply.
retrievalUnits.admission: Document posting preselection may combine section/typed-record groups for declared whole documents, never independent facts or JSONL records. Exact decoded scoring and unit checks follow this conservative preselection.
retrievalUnits.selection: Sparse planning selects bounded units and respects per-document limits. A source unit contributes only its own matched groups. Planner acceptance is checked against final selected coverage, not coverage of discarded records.
retrievalUnits.corroboration: A document unit may contribute corroborating group paths only when a representative of that exact provenance/status/authority unit survives final selection. Another record at the same physical path does not authorize it.
retrievalUnits.boundary: This is an explicit structural retrieval scope, not a compiler call graph or semantic relevance guarantee. No field weights, consumer policies or generated snapshot format change in this correction.
retrievalUnits.nearCompleteHeadingCorroboration: When the existing multi-document body-only supplement is eligible, a section missing one query group may use a non-body match from a sibling section of the same declared document unit. Filename-only matches, independent rows, differing status/authority/provenance and fabricated coverage remain excluded. Indexed candidate and output limits remain unchanged.

diagnostics.matching: Includes policy, independent-expected-path-probe-not-selection scope and document_matched_groups. A path-local score is not a declaration of candidate admission or selection.
diagnostics.ordinary_row_candidate_probe: Reports strict and relaxed posting-stage candidate counts, expected-path admitted row counts and sparse path-probe completeness. When the ordinary clause uses a generated-row scan, admitted rows are unknown/null, not zero. This probe is separate from owner, identifier and document-planner selection.

verification.boundary: These contracts do not promise semantic understanding, runtime truth, or ranking quality on an unmeasured corpus.

prefixCompletion.activation: Disabled for ordinary public query construction. Query length never changes exact lexical terms into prefix matches.
prefixCompletion.boundary: Internal opt-in prefix matching helpers remain bounded; no public autocomplete mode is introduced by this candidate.

fastPrefilter.policy: A necessary ASCII subsequence check and positive lexical word-boundary shortcut may avoid vocabulary allocation. They do not change the canonical lexical match predicate.
fastPrefilter.nativePropertyTest: Core 2.0 assert_lexical_word_match_equivalence compares field matching to indexed vocabulary, including camel boundaries, punctuation and numeric terms. The obsolete atomic-source matcher was removed.

previewRedaction.policy: Redact complete normalized lines before joining, and complete collected preview/summary values before truncation. JSON, JSONL and source declarations follow the same order.
previewRedaction.boundary: This preserves the existing heuristic detector, not a claim that every secret is recognized. It prevents clipping a recognizable credential into a sensitive unrecognizable prefix and keeps assignment detection within its original line boundary.
previewRedaction.verification: Synthetic credential controls cover 280/420/900-byte cutoffs, assignment line boundaries, JSON/JSONL summaries and source declarations.

coverage.rows: matched_group_indices describe that exact returned row, including explicitly marked prefix support; rows never inherit other sections' matches.
coverage.documents: selected_document_paths may describe corroborating rows within the same returned whole-document unit. Paths from discarded units, independent source members, JSONL records or different provenance/status/authority are not credited merely because the physical path survives.
coverage.boundary: Document coverage is lexical retrieval evidence, not semantic completeness, correctness, execution proof or a compiler-resolved dependency.

sourceCorpus.implementation: src/generation.cpp: build_source_scan_corpus reuses build_generated_rows without serialization or publication.
sourceCorpus.projection: src/extraction.cpp: query_fact_row projects decisions and typed references into the same fields as generated-row decoding.
sourceCorpus.invariant: On the same corpus and row threshold, indexed Context and source-scan Context return identical scored sections/facts, source ranges, provenance, match groups and match counts.
sourceCorpus.boundary: This invariant does not equate Brief owner/planner routing with source-scan Brief or legacy raw-line source-scan Search. Those modes are explicit and never an implicit fallback from a corrupt or stale snapshot.
